why_relevant: Operating since 2008 with dedicated finance/banking and IT verticals; hosts employer pages for institutions including Banka Qendrore e Kosovës. Project-manager and implementation postings here are RFP-adjacent signals of upcoming system programmes.

Named in the cell scope; aggregates finance/technology/engineering vacancies in Kosovo. Useful as a redundancy layer: some bank and vendor ads appear here and not on KosovaJob, and cross-board duplication timestamps a hiring burst.

Self-described largest real-time Kosovo employment platform covering finance and technology; carries project-manager and bank vacancies. Tag pages (/tag/konkurse-pune/) give a cheap firehose for monitoring.
Engineering-subcategory feed surfaces technical bank/vendor roles (systems, integration, infrastructure) that name platforms. Faceted subcategory URLs make targeted collection simple.
Aggregator of currently-active Kosovo competitions; acts as a discovery pointer to employers and to boards not yet on the collection list, and helps catch postings before deadline removal.

Cross-border KS/AL board; relevant because several Kosovo banks are Albanian-group subsidiaries (BKT, Credins) whose Tirana-side technical hiring reveals group-level platform choices that cascade to Kosovo.

Gjirafa is the dominant Albanian-language search engine and its jobs vertical indexes vacancies across many Kosovo boards, including small/company-site-only postings. Best used as a meta-search pointer for discovering boards and employers outside the known set.
Classifieds channel used by smaller integrators, POS/ATM service firms and fintech shops that do not post on formal boards — the sub-tier of the payments supply chain that is otherwise invisible.

source_name: Poslovi Infostud — Kosovska Mitrovica job listings (Serbian-language)
why_relevant: The most-used Serbian job site; the Kosovska Mitrovica location feed covers the Serbian-system banking/IT footprint in northern Kosovo (Serbian-parallel institutions, Treasury/Uprava za trezor roles, telecom and IT installers) that Albanian-language boards never carry.

source_name: HelloWorld.rs — IT job board, Kosovska Mitrovica feed
why_relevant: Serbia's main developer-focused board; ads carry explicit technology stacks (frameworks, middleware, DB, integration platforms), which is exactly the technical-footprint leak this cell targets, for the northern-Kosovo and diaspora-delivery segment.

source_name: Asseco SEE — Kosovo (Prishtina) vacancies, BANKING unit
why_relevant: Direct evidence of a regional digital-banking-platform vendor staffing a Prishtina banking delivery unit. Vendor-side hiring volume and role titles are a leading indicator of which Kosovo banks it is delivering to and of an expanding local delivery hub.

source_name: LinkedIn — Kosovo bank & vendor jobs and employee-profile stack traces
why_relevant: Richest single source for platform names: job ads and, more durably, employee profiles/skills at Kosovo banks and their integrators state 'T24', 'Flexcube', 'Way4', 'Oracle', 'Asseco', 'Temenos' explicitly. Kosovo job boards themselves maintain LinkedIn company pages (e.g. Portal Pune), so it doubles as a pointer.

source_name: Google Play Store — Kosovo bank mobile app listings
why_relevant: Package IDs expose the white-label builder outright: ProCredit Kosova ships under 'com.quipugmbh.*' (Quipu GmbH, the ProCredit group IT arm), while BKT ('com.bkt.bktkosovo') and TEB ('com.tebkos.TebMobile') use in-house/group namespaces. Developer name, release cadence, permissions and 'what's new' text date platform migrations.

source_name: Apple App Store — Kosovo bank app listings (seller identity)
why_relevant: The App Store shows the legal 'Seller' entity, which often differs from the bank brand and names the actual development vendor or group IT company; paired with a new app ID (e.g. a 2024-era ProCredit Kosova listing alongside an older m-banking one) it dates a channel-platform replacement.

source_name: εxodus Privacy — Android APK tracker/SDK reports
why_relevant: Analyses APKs and publishes the embedded third-party SDKs and permissions per app version. Applied to Kosovo bank APKs this exposes the analytics, auth, RASP/security and engagement vendors inside the digital channel — vendor relationships never announced publicly.

Lists the libraries an app is built with, giving a second, independent read on a bank app's technology stack (cross-platform framework, push, crash, auth SDKs) and on the developer's whole app portfolio — which reveals white-label vendors serving several banks.

source_name: Open Banking Tracker — Kosovo (XK) provider & API directory
why_relevant: Enumerates the ~15 Kosovo banks with their digital/API footprints — the canonical target list against which to run all hiring and app-store monitoring, and an early indicator of which institutions have developer-facing API programmes (i.e. a modern channel platform).
